title: Add an evidence-aware design alternative explorer
summary: Let a designer compare multiple screen, component and flow alternatives against responsive, accessibility and repository constraints before selecting a proposal.
acceptance_criteria: The experience starts from a concrete user question and the smallest useful decision, not a generic chat surface or exhaustive setup.
Every recommendation references the exact scenario, state, evidence, source revision and constraints used to derive it.
The UI separates observed fact, user input, derived signal, heuristic, forecast, preference and policy.
Confidence, uncertainty, missing evidence, stale input, unsupported state and model or rule disagreement are visible before a user decides.
At least one meaningful alternative and a no-action or gather-more-evidence path are available with trade-offs.
The user can edit assumptions and constraints, rerun the scenario, accept, reject, postpone or preserve a dissenting alternative.
No recommendation executes a command, changes source truth, sends data, controls hardware, schedules an external action or grants permission automatically.
The accepted choice creates an immutable decision receipt with scope, rationale, source scenario, affected objects and revocation or correction posture.
Offline, stale, partial, blocked, inconclusive, failed and recovered states remain distinct and never appear as successful recommendation output.
Sensitive health, family, customer, financial, media, credential or location data remains local or explicitly consent-scoped and minimized.
The experience avoids manipulation, shame, artificial urgency, hidden tracking, forced personalization and false precision.
Explicit feedback distinguishes factual correction, preference, perceived outcome, uncertainty, safety concern and product suggestion.
Accessibility covers keyboard or platform navigation, screen-reader hierarchy, scalable text, non-color status cues, reduced motion and accessible explanations.
Locale-aware copy, dates, times, currencies, units and pluralization are verified for supported languages.
Deterministic tests and visual/runtime fixtures cover normal, minimal-data, stale, offline, conflicting, rejected, reset and recovery paths.
The strongest repository-native test, build, accessibility, scenario and zero-warning gates pass.
The explorer shows baseline and alternatives side by side with exact constraint, source and behavior differences.
Critique distinguishes deterministic violation, design heuristic, product assumption and missing evidence.
The user can preserve rejected alternatives and rationale as design-decision evidence.
Selecting an alternative generates a structured proposal and never initiates Codex work without a separate accepted ticket and Work Package.

agent_notes: Portfolio Intelligence & Simulation Wave 6; evidence-backed scenario and explainable-decision planning ticket.
Estimated effort: L to XL after all prerequisites; split implementation into bounded Work Packages.
Implementation risk: medium-high because deterministic replay, privacy, uncertainty and product decisions must remain honest.
Non-scope: Do not create an unconstrained general-purpose chatbot, auto-execute recommendations, or infer sensitive facts not explicitly provided by the user or domain contract.
Alternative considered and rejected: Show a single opaque AI recommendation — rejected because the user needs evidence, assumptions, alternatives, uncertainty, control and a durable decision record.
Run a fresh delta review against the current default branch before publication or implementation.
Wave 8 portfolio reassessment: retain-conditional; priority band later. Replay and scenario evidence can reduce risk, but it must follow deterministic core behavior and real evidence.
Wave 10 final rationalization: retain-research-with-cap; portfolio band later. Keep a bounded scenario and decision-support runway where it reduces material risk.
Wave 11 execution reconciliation: `optional-reference-or-research`. Use the Wave 11 implementation program as the delivery entry point while preserving this ticket's evidence and intent.

Wave 12 deep reassessment: decision `retain-research`, relevance `later`, current priority `medium`, execution gate `real baseline, deterministic scenario, and no displacement of active delivery`. Replay and simulation can reduce material risk after deterministic behavior and current evidence exist.
Wave 13 human-validation reassessment: `retain-risk-research` / `later` / priority `medium`. Simulation and recommendations follow real product evidence, not precede it.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid-research-or-reference`; publication `publish-as-proposed-backlog`; implementation sequence `later`. Simulation and recommendations follow real product evidence, not precede it.
